name: Daylight as Multi-Channel Stimulus with Convergent Benefit
short_description: Natural daylight simultaneously provides six mechanistic benefits through partially independent pathways; convergence produces effects larger than any single channel
structural_pattern: Natural daylight simultaneously provides six distinguishable benefits through partially independent mechanisms: (1) circadian entrainment (ipRGC → SCN → melatonin/cortisol alignment; L2), (2) acute alerting (ipRGC → brainstem arousal centers → cortical activation), (3) visual comfort and color fidelity (broadband spectrum → accurate color constancy → low chromatic PE), (4) view and environmental connection (window → outdoor scene → soft fascination, T27; environmental monitoring → threat reduction, T5), (5) dynamic temporal variation (sun movement, clouds, weather → moderate sustained luminance PE, L1 Goldilocks range), and (6) temporal orientation (light quality encodes time of day and season → temporal prediction congruence). The convergence of all six channels produces effects substantially larger than any single channel alone.
higher_order_principle: Multi-channel convergence applied to daylight. Parallels AX6 (Multi-Modal PE Integration) and the BRECVEMA convergence principle (M16). No artificial lighting system that matches daylight on only one parameter will replicate the full daylight effect, because the effect is a product of simultaneous activation across channels.

channels.mechanism: ipRGC → locus coeruleus, dorsal raphe → cortical arousal

channels.name: color_fidelity

causal_links.evidence_base: Channel 1. Via L2. Daylight provides high melanopic irradiance from above during biological day.

Channel 2. ipRGC → locus coeruleus, dorsal raphe → cortical arousal. Operates within minutes. Vandewalle et al. (2009) demonstrated light-driven activation of brainstem arousal and limbic structures via fMRI.
Channel 3. Broadband daylight spectrum → minimal chromatic PE (Hurlbert, 2007). Surfaces appear as expected; color constancy operates within its evolved operating range.
Channel 4. Via T27 (DMN/soft fascination) and T5 (threat reduction through environmental monitoring). View provides visual access, depth, and natural scene content.
Channel 5. Via L1 (luminance PE). Sun movement, cloud passage, and weather variation create continuous low-to-moderate luminance PE that sustains engagement without causing fatigue.
Channel 6. Light color temperature and directionality encode time of day. Loss of this signal in windowless spaces may contribute to temporal disorientation.

The convergence effect. Heschong (2002) 20% math improvement cannot be attributed to any single channel. The multiplicative convergence principle predicts that blocking any single channel substantially reduces the total effect.

channel_weights.note: Expert-estimated weights from Panel L-II — VERY PRELIMINARY, not empirical values

circadian_L2.evidence: Figueiro's work shows circadian-optimized electric lighting recovers 40–60% of daylight effect on sleep and alertness

view_VIEW1.evidence: Heschong finding that view content predicts performance independently of illumination; nature view literature

luminance_contrast_L1.evidence: Daylit spaces have more varied and directional luminance distributions than most artificial lighting

ecological_CCT_L4.evidence: Contested mechanism — if merely arousal, this weight is absorbed into circadian and contrast channels

dynamic_variation_L5.evidence: Preliminary mechanism — estimated contribution based on occupant satisfaction gap

super_additivity.meaning: Full-daylight effect is ~15–25% larger than would be predicted by summing individual channels
super_additivity.note: Consistent with convergence principle in VIEW1 and MAT4 but not directly measured

channel_separation_status.view_separable_from_light: Confirmed — Heschong (2002) view content predicts performance independently of illumination level
channel_separation_status.circadian_separable_from_visual: Confirmed — Figueiro's work shows circadian-optimized electric lighting works in windowless environments (but smaller effects)
channel_separation_status.dynamics_separable_from_average_illumina: Partially confirmed — Chamilothori's moving vs static sunlight patches (but magnitude of L5 independent contribution unknown)
channel_separation_status.full_factorial_separation: NOT YET CONDUCTED — highest priority for L-III

assessment_tools.integrated_multi_channel: No integrated assessment tool yet exists

calibration_parameters.calibration_source: Panel L-II (Doc 49) — Heschong, de Kort, Foster expert estimation

scope_conditions: Applies to any building with windows providing daylight access
Effect magnitude depends on daylight availability (climate, orientation, window-to-wall ratio, glazing type)
Deep-plan buildings may provide daylight to perimeter zones but not core zones → spatial inequality
Seasonal variation: high-latitude winter reduces all six channels
moderators: Window design: size, placement, glazing transmittance, shading determine how much of each channel is delivered
View quality: natural outdoor scene > urban roofscape > lightwell > interior partition
Occupant position relative to window: daylight benefits decrease with distance from facade
Task demands: high visual-task environments may require electric lighting supplement even with good daylight
Glare control: uncontrolled direct sun can negate daylight benefits through discomfort

interactions.nature: L2 is Channel 1 of L3. L3 embeds L2 within the broader multi-channel framework.
L1 is Channel 5 of L3 (dynamic luminance variation). L3 embeds L1's Goldilocks principle within the broader convergence.
T27 is Channel 4 of L3. Window views provide soft fascination → DMN re-engagement → attention restoration.
L3 is the daylight-specific instance of the multi-channel convergence principle formalized in AX6.
T5 is Channel 4 of L3. Windows provide environmental monitoring → threat reduction.
